subject: Private Offer: pre-approval playbook + term options for NovaMed

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood private offer — proposal and approval checklist

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is our initial private-offer proposal (Redwood_PO_Proposal_NovaMed_v1.pdf) with two term options we think map to NovaMed's org constraints: a 12-month standard commit, and an 11-month staggered-activation alternative that can help align with your fiscal year close.

Two asks from our side so we can move to private-offer creation in AWS Marketplace:
- Who needs to sign/approve on your side (roles/titles)? Is procurement + finance sufficient, or will each BU (Clinical Ops / Dev / IT Security) require signoff?
- Do you have an internal PO template we should populate (we can push a seller-friendly template if that helps expedite approvals)?

Operational notes we recommend:
- If procurement wants a shorter visible term, we can propose an 11-month term with a pro-rated month 12 true-up to reduce CFO friction.
- We can include an evidence pack (SOC2 summary, data-residency notes) in the private-offer packet for procurement review.

Proposed next steps: you confirm approver list and preferred term option, we prepare the private offer and PO template, then schedule a 20-min sync with procurement this week.

Thanks,

Hi Lauren,

Appreciate the clear options. Quick answers from our side:
- Procurement + FP&A will need to sign off. For larger line items, our Clinical Ops head signs only for budget confirmation but not procurement approval.
- Our procurement team prefers to see a populated PO template; I can share our standard PO but it often stalls legal review.

About the term: FP&A prefers annual commitments for forecast stability. Would you consider an 11-month option only if we can get a discount or ramp credits?

I can loop in procurement (procurement@novamed.com) — could you provide a Redwood-populated PO template and a short list of the exact evidence items? Procurement will want SOC2, data retention policy, and the AWS Marketplace activation steps spelled out.

Thanks,

Adding a few practical pre-approval ideas that have helped reduce buyer latency on similar marketplace deals:

1) Pre-approved PO stub: we can fill your PO with the final line-items and terms so procurement only has to drop in an internal signatory rather than re-key the commercial terms. This typically shortens review by 3–5 business days.

2) Delegated approver matrix: if multiple BUs are informational-only (e.g., Clinical Ops confirms budget but doesn't sign), call that out in a one-page matrix. Procurement/legal like the clarity.

3) Offer a 2-tier incentive: 12-month list price, or 11-month with a 7% activation credit (applied at month 1) to satisfy FP&A's stability needs while giving them near-term flexibility. We can label the second option as "11m discounted activation" in the private offer.

4) Evidence pack: SOC2 Type II summary, short data residency note, and a one-pager on activation steps (what NovaMed will see during AWS Marketplace activation + how we handle billing). I'll attach our short activation playbook to the follow-up.

If procurement can confirm whether the contract requires an entity-level signature vs. PO-only activation, we can align the DocuSign flow accordingly.

Happy to join a procurement sync if that helps. Lauren, once you have NovaMed's PO template, I can drop our seller-populated version and Jordan can attach the actual PO stub.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Mid-Market Sales | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
